48.0.s.en: (1) Jacob's illness and his blessing of Joseph

48.0.0.en: Joseph heard of his father's illness and felt that it might be his final illness, so he hurried with his two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, so that Jacob might bless them before his death. When Jacob learned that Joseph had come, he strengthened himself despite his weakness and sat up on his bed.

48.1.0.en: An everlasting possession: not only for the descendants of Jacob in Canaan, but because Canaan is a symbol of the Kingdom of Heaven, which is inherited by those who believe in Christ, who is of the seed of Jacob. The possession is not limited to the earthly possession that was fulfilled in the Old Testament, but it is a symbol of the heavenly possession that is fulfilled in the New Testament. Jacob declared to Joseph that God had appeared to him at Luz, which was later called Bethel, when he was fleeing from the face of Esau, and then a second time when he returned from his uncle Laban, and that He blessed him and promised him numerous offspring and the inheritance of the land of Canaan. So he declares to him that the blessing he would give to him and to his children is from God, the source of blessings. In the same way, the Church blesses her children by the Holy Spirit who dwells in her.

48.1.1.en: Enjoy the blessings of the Church through the prayers and the Holy Sacraments, so that you may become a source of blessing to everyone you meet and every place you go to, and so be the light of the world and the salt of the earth.

48.2.0.en: Jacob gave Joseph's blessing two portions instead of the one portion that he gave to each of his brothers, because of his love and Joseph's distinction in forgiveness and giving. In this way Joseph became the firstborn (1 Chr 5:1) in place of Reuben, who lost his birthright by lying with his father's wife (ch. 35:21-26). So the two sons of Joseph are in their inheritance like the rest of Joseph's brothers in the inheritance. As for the children whom God would give to Joseph after Ephraim and Manasseh, they would inherit in the Promised Land following their brothers Ephraim and Manasseh; that is, they would have no third portion, because Joseph's portion became the two portions of Ephraim and Manasseh.

48.3.0.en: As Jacob was blessing Joseph, he remembered Joseph's mother Rachel, whom he loved very much and whom he had buried beside Ephrath, which is Bethlehem. He did so to bind the heart of his son Joseph to the Land of Promise, Canaan, so that he would feel that he was a stranger in the land of Egypt, even though he ruled over it.

48.4.s.en: (2) Jacob's blessing of Ephraim and Manasseh

48.4.0.en: Jacob's eyes were dim with age, so he asked Joseph about the two men who were with him. Joseph was then 56 years old, while Ephraim and Manasseh were young men in their early twenties. Joseph said to him that they were his sons whom God had given him in Egypt, and then he brought them near to his father, who embraced them and kissed them.

48.5.0.en: Jacob declared his joy at seeing and embracing Joseph's two sons, and said to him, "I had hoped to see you, and God has granted me not only to see you but your children also." When Joseph took the two grandsons out from between Jacob's knees and arms, for he had been holding them close, rejoicing at meeting them, the two grandsons then bowed down to their grandfather out of respect and reverence. The word "bowed" appears in the Septuagint as "they bowed down."

48.6.0.en: Joseph brought his two sons near, Manasseh the firstborn at Jacob's right hand and Ephraim the younger at his left, so that the greater blessing would be given to the firstborn. But God had made known to Jacob that the younger would be a greater blessing than the firstborn, so he laid his right hand on Ephraim and his left on Manasseh. In this way his hands formed the shape of a cross, a symbol of all the blessings of the New Testament that come through the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

48.7.0.en: Jacob blessed Joseph's two sons with the following blessings:

48.7.1.en: 1- The blessing of the God who shepherded him and his fathers: He will shepherd them with His care.

48.7.2.en: 2- The blessing of the God who delivered him by His angel from many afflictions, such as his exposure to being killed by Esau, then Laban's exploitation and pursuit of him, and his protection from the surrounding tribes after the killing of the tribe of Shechem: He blesses the two grandsons and delivers them from every affliction.

48.7.3.en: 3- They will receive the blessing of the name of their grandfather Jacob and of his fathers Isaac and Abraham, when they inherit the Promised Land as God promised.

48.8.0.en: Joseph was displeased that the greater blessing was given to the younger Ephraim, and he thought that this was because of the weakness of his father Jacob's eyesight. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's, and said to him that Manasseh was the firstborn. Jacob answered him, "God has made known to me that Manasseh will be blessed, but his younger brother will be more fruitful and a greater blessing than his brother." This indeed happened, as appears from the history of the people of Ephraim in the following:

48.8.1.en: 1- Great men came from him, such as Joshua the son of Nun and Samuel the prophet.

48.8.2.en: 2- His number was large. In the first census taken in the days of Moses, the number of those enrolled for war from Ephraim was 40,500, while that of Manasseh was 32,200 (Num 1:32-35).

48.8.3.en: 3- Shiloh, where the tabernacle of meeting was set up for a period of time, was one of the cities of Ephraim (1 Sam 1:3).

48.8.4.en: 4- The tribe of Manasseh was divided in its dwelling: half of it lived east of the Jordan River and mixed with the idolaters, while the other half lived west of it, which led to the weakening of the tribe.

48.9.0.en: Jacob blessed Joseph's two sons, and they became a blessing, so much so that they were used as a byword for blessing, and it would be said, "God bless you like Ephraim and Manasseh." He put Ephraim before Manasseh because he would become a greater blessing, and the kingdom of Israel was sometimes called Ephraim because of the greatness of the tribe of Ephraim.

48.9.1.en: God gives His blessing to the great or the small, so be strong, believe in God, and ask for His help and blessing, however small, despised or neglected you may be, for by God's blessing and your faith you will become great.

48.10.0.en: Before he died, Jacob assured his son Joseph of God's promise to give them the land of Canaan, and that He would bring them back to it from Egypt so that they might inherit it.

48.11.0.en: He told Joseph that he had given him a portion (a share) greater than that of his brothers, as he had said before that he had made an inheritance for Ephraim and Manasseh like the rest of Joseph's brothers. Here he adds a new piece of information: that he had taken some land from the Amorites, not only the plot that he had bought from Hamor, the father of Shechem, but it may be that some of the Amorites had attacked his plot of land there, so he fought them, recovered his land, and took some of their neighboring lands. He gave the land and the well that was in it to Joseph, as is mentioned in (Jn 4:5, 6). Jacob's blessing of his sons

49.0.0.en: In the last days: that is, the future.

49.0.1.en: Jacob called his twelve sons to give them his farewell charges before he died, and to bless them and prophesy to them about their future.

49.1.0.en: My might and the beginning of my strength: the firstborn represents strength and blessing.

49.1.2.en: The excellency of dignity and the excellency of power: the firstborn is expected to lift up his father's head by his good conduct and distinction. Jacob praises his son Reuben, whose name means "son of the vision," saying that he was expected to represent the greatness and loftiness of his father, and that in him were the fullness of blessing and strength. So it is a rebuke within the manner of a commendation.

49.1.3.en: Be gentle in rebuking others and praise them with kind words, so that you convey to them the meaning you intend, which is that they leave their sins and walk uprightly, without wounding their feelings.

49.2.0.en: Boiling over like water: unstable; you rise like water that boils with its bubbles, then cools and sinks. You shall not excel: you have no preeminence over your brothers.

49.2.1.en: Simeon and Levi are brothers: Simeon is the forefather of the scribes and Levi the forefather of the priests.

49.2.2.en: Jacob continued his rebuke of Reuben, but in more direct words, since he blamed him for his instability, like water that boils over and then cools, and for losing preeminence over his brothers because he fell into a shameful sin, which was his lying with his father's concubine Bilhah.

49.3.0.en: Weapons of injustice are their swords: their wrong against the tribe of Shechem, all of whose men they killed because of the sin of one person, Shechem.

49.3.1.en: Let my soul not enter: I cannot sit between them, because of their anger and their evil.

49.3.2.en: Let not my honor be united: my soul would be humbled and I would be without honor if I sat among them, because of their great evil. They killed a man: Shechem and his tribe.

49.3.3.en: In their consent: when they pretended gentleness and agreement with Hamor and Shechem, they deceived them.

49.3.4.en: They hamstrung an ox: they struck it at the bottom of its leg near the foot, so that it fell, and they killed it. The ox symbolizes the strong man, that is, Shechem and the men of his tribe.

49.3.5.en: The brothers Simeon and Levi were united in the anger and vengeance that appeared in their killing of the men of the tribe of Shechem (ch. 34). Therefore Jacob, the man of God, declares that he finds no rest in associating with them, because of their dreadful evil and their fury that knows no limit.

49.4.0.en: Jacob denounces their anger and vengeance because it is severe and cruel, and God's punishment for them is that they will be scattered in their inheritance among the tribes of Israel and will not have a unified territory. The tribe of Simeon gradually dwindled, as appears from the two censuses taken by Moses (Num 1, 26), and when they entered the Promised Land under Joshua they had no portion of their own, but possessed some parts of the land of Judah (Josh 19). As for the tribe of Levi, it had no portion in a particular region of the Promised Land, but only some scattered cities, because it was consecrated to service (Num 18:20, 35:1-8).

49.5.0.en: Judah: his name means praise. His father prophesies to him that his brothers will glorify him and give thanks to him, and that he will be strong and will strike his enemies on the back of the neck, that is, they will flee before him, and his brothers will bow down to him, because from him comes David the prophet, and his descendants are the kings of the kingdom of Judah; and then from his descendants comes also Christ, the King of kings, to whom the whole world bows down.

49.6.0.en: A lion's whelp: a cub, that is, the young son of the lion.

49.6.1.en: From the prey you have gone up: strong like the lion that devours its enemies and goes up victorious in wars.

49.6.2.en: He stooped down, he couched: he settled after his victory.

49.6.3.en: Who shall rouse him up: no one can disturb him or move him from his rest.

49.6.4.en: He likens him to the lion, the king of the beasts, in his strength and his victory over all his enemies, and then he settles, and everyone fears him and keeps away from him. And from the descendants of Judah comes Christ, who is victorious over Satan and binds him when He stoops down and couches on the cross, and no one can stop His redemption, His death and His resurrection. No one can raise Christ up, but it is He who raises Himself on the third day.

49.7.0.en: Sceptre: a golden rod that kings hold as a declaration of their reign.

49.7.1.en: Lawgiver: the one who decides laws and commandments.

49.7.2.en: From between his feet: from his descendants.

49.7.3.en: Shiloh: it means the One to whom everything belongs, or the Peacemaker, or the Savior.

49.7.5.en: He declares that from the tribe of Judah will come David the king, from whose descendants come the kings over Jerusalem, until we reach Christ the Savior, who is Shiloh, and who reigns over the hearts of those who believe in Him from all the peoples of the world, and not only the believers from among the Jews.

49.8.0.en: The vine: that is, the grapevine or the vine tree.

49.8.1.en: The blood of grapes: the juice of the grape that becomes wine.

49.8.2.en: Darker in the eyes from wine: a figure for much drinking of wine, so that the eyes sparkle and are able to see sharply.

49.8.3.en: Whiter in the teeth from milk: a figure for the abundance of milk and of the flocks that yield it, which symbolizes the words of Christ, who comes from his descendants, and which nourish like milk.

49.8.4.en: He prophesies to him the many good things, symbolized by the abundance of vines and the grape juice that comes from them, and by the many flocks that yield milk: the land will be fertile and he will possess many flocks. This also symbolizes the blood of Christ the Redeemer, which we receive in the Church in the sacrament of Holy Communion.

49.8.5.en: When God gives you material blessings, take care to thank Him and to lift your eyes to the greater spiritual blessings in the Kingdom of Heaven, so that you are not absorbed in material things, but they lift you up to the love of God and to clinging to Him.

49.9.0.en: The haven of the sea: the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, west of the Jordan River.

49.9.1.en: A haven of ships: that is, the ports.

49.9.2.en: His border shall be unto Zidon: it reaches the city of Sidon, which lies on the Mediterranean about 25 miles south of present-day Beirut. Jacob prophesied that Zebulun would dwell on the coast of the Mediterranean and work in trade and mix with the nations, and that this would expose him to the worship of idols and to imitating their corruption; but when he believes in Christ, who preached in this region, he becomes a light to the world and a preacher of Christ (Mt 4:15, 16).

49.10.0.en: Shall judge his people: shall rule himself.

49.10.1.en: Dan is the first son of a maidservant, for he is the son of Bilhah the maidservant, but he is counted as a tribe like the rest of the tribes, ruling himself.

49.11.1.en: In the way .. in the path: he pursues his enemies with cunning and is victorious over them.

49.11.2.en: That biteth the horse heels, so that his rider shall fall backward: with shrewdness he strips the enemy of his weapons and his strength and so triumphs over him.

49.11.3.en: He likened Dan to the serpent because he was characterized by cunning and shrewdness. He was not distinguished by the great number of his soldiers or by military strength, but he won by shrewdness combined with courage.

49.12.0.en: When he likened him to the serpent, he remembered Satan, the first serpent, and longed for the Messiah the Savior.

49.12.1.en: When afflictions come upon you or you fall into various sins, do not despair, but rise and ask for God's help, and if the affliction lasts long, wait for God's salvation, for He will never leave you.

49.13.0.en: A troop shall overcome him: enemies attack him.

49.13.1.en: He shall overcome at the last: he pursues his enemies after they have withdrawn from him and is victorious over them in the end. The tribe of Gad lived east of the Jordan, so it was exposed to many attacks by the Ammonites and the Amorites, who would overcome it, but it would return, pursue them and defeat them, and take much spoil from them.

49.14.0.en: His bread shall be fat: his good things are many.

49.14.1.en: Royal dainties: the precious goods that kings and great men seek.

49.14.2.en: Asher dwelt in a fertile land on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, in which olive trees were plentiful, so he obtained abundant harvests, from which he exported to the rest of the tribes. And because he lived beside the sea, he worked in trade, exporting and trading in the precious goods that the great men of the whole world seek. Moses the prophet also prophesied about him that he would dip his foot in oil because of the abundance of olive trees (Deut 33:24).

49.15.0.en: A hind: the female of the deer, a kind of gazelle that is very swift in movement.

49.15.2.en: Goodly words: his dealings are good and he is understanding.

49.15.3.en: He likens him to the female gazelle, swift in movement and unbound, because his land was fertile and he went out freely to work in it and enjoy prosperity; but in danger he would hasten to fight the enemies, and his dealings were good with the rest of the tribes around him.

49.15.4.en: Take care to speak well and to be kind in dealing with those around you, so that you build good relationships with them and live in peace, and are able to influence them and draw them to Christ.

49.16.0.en: He describes his beloved son Joseph as a fruitful branch from his father's tree: if his father had many descendants, he too would be fruitful. He is ever green and full of life because he is by a well of water, that is, spiritual and material blessings continue for him, as do loftiness and exaltation, since he became ruler over Egypt.

49.17.0.en: Have sorely grieved him: they persecuted him and afflicted him with bitterness, that is, distress.

49.17.1.en: The archers: those who were hostile to him, such as his brothers, or Potiphar's wife, or Potiphar himself, who cast him into prison.

49.17.2.en: Joseph was exposed to many persecutions from those around him.

49.18.0.en: The mighty God of Jacob: the beloved and strong God.

49.18.2.en: The shepherd: the guide and leader.

49.18.3.en: The stone of Israel: the strong helper of Israel.

49.18.4.en: Joseph was able to stand firm by the help of Almighty God, who supports him from heaven, shepherds him and gives him success. So he stood firm in a pure life with God and was strengthened, and did not submit to sin, but passed successfully through all afflictions and became ruler over all Egypt, and even managed its affairs with wisdom and skill.

49.19.0.en: Blessings of heaven: the rains and the dew.

49.19.1.en: Blessings of the deep that lieth under: the rivers that water his land.

49.19.2.en: Of the breasts and of the womb: abundance of offspring and their strength, because he is nourished much from the breasts, that is, material blessings. He prophesied and asked for him God's blessings from heaven in the rains, and from the earth in the rivers, and abundance of offspring and their strength. The strength of the two tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh appeared in (Deut 33:13-17, Josh 17:17, 18).

49.20.0.en: Utmost: the summit of what a person desires and longs for.

49.20.2.en: Everlasting: existing from of old, that is, from a long time ago. The meaning is that he receives blessings to the utmost of what he desires.

49.20.3.en: Separate from his brethren: set apart and distinguished from his brothers by his righteousness.

49.20.4.en: He told him that the blessings that would come upon him were greater than the blessings that his father and his grandfather had received, and that they would be to the utmost possible, because of his distinction and his righteousness.

49.20.5.en: Hold fast to your faith even if some wrong you and you endure afflictions through no fault of your own; stand firm in your principles and God will support you, and in the end you will receive inexpressible blessings that satisfy you on earth, and then you will enjoy them forever.

49.21.0.en: He describes him as courageous like the wolf that devours the spoil in the morning, and then, when it settles in the evening, he and his children eat of the prey as he divides it among them. It is said of his warriors and their mastery of war that they "could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss" (Judg 20:16). Thus Jacob prophesied to his sons, showing their various characteristics and warning them so that they would repent of their sins and walk uprightly. These are prophecies and teachings for all believers, so that they may guard against the devil's snares and hold fast to the virtues. His teachings and directions can be summarized as follows:

49.21.1.en: 1- Reuben: guard against pride and lust.

49.21.2.en: 2- Simeon and Levi: guard against plots, anger and vengeance.

49.21.3.en: 3- Zebulun: guard against mixing with the wicked, and turn instead to preaching to them.

49.21.4.en: 4- Issachar: he calls him to endurance and perseverance.

49.21.5.en: 5- Dan: he warns him against craftiness and cunning.

49.21.6.en: 6- Gad: he calls him to hope in the struggle and not to despair.

49.21.7.en: 7- Asher: he wishes him abundant blessings.

49.21.8.en: 8- Naphtali: he praises him for his good relationships and his understanding with others.

49.21.9.en: 9- Joseph: he wishes him continual growth.

49.22.1.en: The preceding blessings are those with which Jacob blessed his sons, who became the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel.

49.23.0.en: He asked all his sons, as he had asked Joseph before in (ch. 47:29-31), to bury him in Canaan, in the cave of Machpelah, which is in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah were buried.

49.24.0.en: Jacob finally died at the age of 147 years, and although he died in a foreign land, his spirit was gathered to his people, that is, his believing fathers, who were awaiting in hope the redemption of Christ and His resurrection, that they might be raised up to Paradise.

49.24.1.en: Look to the end of your life, which is death, so that you do not accept sin or become careless with it. And your remembrance of death every morning lifts you to heavenly readiness, so that you walk in all that pleases God and give love to everyone you meet.

49.24.2.en: We observe that Jacob is a type of Christ in the following:

49.24.3.en: 1- The Holy Bible testified of Jacob that he was a perfect man (ch. 25:27), and Christ was perfect and said, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (Jn 8:26).

49.24.4.en: 2- Jacob lived as a stranger, dwelling in tents, and was a stranger with his uncle and then in Egypt, and he described his life as the days of his pilgrimage; and Christ lived detached from the world throughout His life.

49.24.5.en: 3- Jacob received the birthright and the blessing, and Christ is the firstborn among many brethren and is the hypostasis of wisdom and blessing.

49.24.6.en: 4- Jacob was exploited by his uncle Laban, but God rescued him from his hands; and the Jews wronged Christ, persecuted Him and crucified Him, but God raised Him, that is, He rose by His divinity.

49.24.7.en: 5- Jacob was deceived by his sons in the killing of the tribe of Shechem and in the selling of Joseph; and Christ was wounded by His beloved ones, and all those close to Him abandoned Him at the cross.

49.24.8.en: Here we present a summary of the life of Jacob, which is:

49.24.9.en: 1- Jacob the unborn child in his mother's womb (ch. 25).

49.24.10.en: 2- Jacob buys the birthright from Esau (ch. 25).

49.24.13.en: 5- Jacob marries, begets sons and works for his uncle (chs. 29, 30).

49.24.14.en: 6- God delivers Jacob from the pursuit of his uncle Laban (ch. 31).

49.24.16.en: 8- Jacob's meeting and reconciliation with Esau (ch. 33).

49.24.17.en: 9- Shechem's assault on Dinah, Jacob's daughter, and her brothers' vengeance upon them (ch. 34).

49.24.19.en: 11- Jacob and his beloved son Joseph (chs. 37-48).

49.24.20.en: 12- Jacob's blessings to his sons and his death. (ch. 49) The burial of Jacob and the death of Joseph
